a.label: Clear Intent: The Government Coverup of the UFO Experience (1984)

edges.label: Documentary method versus anonymous-testimony method
edges.note: The two bodies of work are contemporaneous and methodologically opposite: 'Clear Intent' sources every claim to a released government document, the Status Reports to protected anonymous informants. Reasoning: the difference in grade this board assigns them is entirely a difference in sourcing, not in subject matter.

edges.label: FUFOR funded Stringfield's later Status Reports
edges.note: Stringfield names the Fund for UFO Research first in the Status Report VII acknowledgements, thanking it for past funding.

a.label: J. Allen Hynek Center for UFO Studies (CUFOS)

edges.label: CUFOS cooperated with and advised the Status Report series
edges.note: Stringfield acknowledges CUFOS cooperation in Status Report VII and records consulting its scientific director on 6 November 1993 about the Roswell body count.

edges.label: Randle's case-by-case surveys audit Stringfield's corpus
edges.note: 'A History of UFO Crashes' (1995) and 'Crash: When UFOs Fall From the Sky' (2010) revisit the Status Report cases with named sourcing where it exists and rejection where it does not. Reasoning: comparison of case lists.

edges.label: MUFON symposium platform and publisher for Reports I and II
edges.note: Report I was delivered at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton on 29 July 1978; Report II was published by MUFON in January 1980. Stringfield served as MUFON's director of public relations.

edges.label: Authored the seven-part Status Report series
edges.note: Stringfield wrote and self-published or placed all seven Status Reports between July 1978 and February 1994. Title and copyright pages of the original printings attest authorship, dates and, for Report VI, the Cincinnati imprint.

a.label: Majic Eyes Only: Earth's Encounters with Extraterrestrial Technology (2005)

edges.label: The catalogue inherits Stringfield's case base
edges.note: A substantial share of 'Majic Eyes Only' entries trace back through Stringfield's anonymised Status Report cases, so the catalogue inherits their provenance limits. Reasoning: an index cannot be graded above its sources.

edges.label: Stringfield revived Aztec as a real retrieval in the late 1970s
edges.note: After two decades in which ufologists treated Aztec as dead, Stringfield argued the incident was real and that the craft was one of many held by the US military; Status Report V lists Aztec alongside Roswell, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County.

b.label: Del Rio / Mexican border claim, 1948 or 1950

edges.label: Status Report chronology indexes Del Rio as Item B-7
edges.note: The consolidated chronology in Status Report III lists Item B-7 of Status Report II as '1948 or 1950: Mexico, near Del Rio, Texas. Air Force officer observed crashed craft and one body.'

edges.label: Status Report III printed the 1980 'Fritz Werner' Q&A on Kingman
edges.note: Stringfield wrote to Raymond Fowler on 11 August 1980 for access to Fowler's pseudonymous source; the answers are dated 2 September 1980 and are printed verbatim in Status Report III.
